extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multimodal evaluation benchmark for assessing multimodal large language models on video understanding, consisting of 900 videos and 2,700 expert-annotated multiple-choice QA pairs across diverse domains, durations, and modalities including subtitles and audio.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in three stages: collecting raw videos from YouTube across a predefined domain hierarchy, annotating each video with three multiple-choice QA pairs, and conducting manual quality review including cross-checking by a different annotator and filtering text-answerable questions using Gemini 1.5 Pro.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not all videos have subtitles; the dataset contains 744 videos with subtitles out of 900 total videos, while all 900 have audio.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube, along with associated meta-information such as subtitles when available and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions that could be answered from text alone were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro and returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were organized by a domain hierarchy with 6 domains and 30 categories, collected across short, medium, and long duration ranges, and associated subtitles and audio were obtained when available.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive vision-language research experience watched each full video and created three multiple-choice questions per video, each with four candidate options. A different annotator then reviewed each QA pair for clarity, answerability, logical consistency, and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality analysis included manual review by a second annotator and automatic filtering of text-only answerable questions using Gemini 1.5 Pro; the paper reports Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support future research and development toward more capable and robust multimodal large language models for video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset aims for relatively balanced distributions of video durations and answer options to reduce bias in evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Not all videos include subtitles, and long videos present greater difficulty due to more reasoning-heavy tasks, sparse frame sampling in some models, and challenges in long-context understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal large language models on video understanding tasks, including both image-based and video-based MLLMs, under different modality settings such as frames only, frames with subtitles, and frames with audio.
